source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Morphology of Flowering Plants
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Pneumatophores that grow upward for gaseous exchange are found in
questions.explanation: Mangroves such as Rhizophora and Avicennia develop negatively geotropic breathing roots.

questions.stem: The potato tuber is a modified
questions.explanation: Eyes of the potato are nodes with buds, proving it is a stem tuber.

questions.stem: Reticulate venation is a characteristic feature of the leaves of
questions.explanation: Dicot leaves typically have a net-like vein pattern; monocots usually show parallel veins.

questions.stem: In garden pea, the tendrils that help the plant to climb are modified
questions.explanation: Upper leaflets of the pinnate pea leaf become tendrils.

questions.stem: In a racemose inflorescence the flowers open in
options: a strictly single terminal flower only
a closed cyme that stops the axis
questions.explanation: The main axis grows continuously and the oldest flowers are at the base (acropetal).

questions.stem: A flower that can be divided into two equal halves only in one plane is
questions.explanation: Zygomorphic (bilateral) flowers, as in pea and gulmohur, have one plane of symmetry.

questions.stem: Vexillary (papilionaceous) aestivation is characteristic of
questions.explanation: In Fabaceae the posterior standard petal overlaps two wings, which overlap the keel.

questions.stem: Diadelphous stamens (9 + 1) are a diagnostic feature of
questions.explanation: Nine stamens unite into a bundle and the tenth remains free in the pea family.

questions.stem: Parietal placentation, with ovules on the inner ovary wall, is seen in
questions.explanation: Brassicaceae (mustard, Argemone) have a unilocular ovary with parietal placentation.

questions.stem: The characteristic fruit of the pea family (Fabaceae) is a
questions.explanation: A legume (pod) dehisces along both sutures; siliqua is Brassicaceae.

questions.stem: Prop roots that hang from branches and prop the tree are typical of
questions.explanation: Banyan produces pillar-like adventitious prop roots; maize has stilt roots from lower nodes.

questions.stem: Twisted aestivation of petals is seen in
questions.explanation: In china rose, cotton and lady’s finger each petal overlaps the next in one direction.

questions.stem: A trimerous flower with six tepals and six stamens is typical of
questions.explanation: Liliaceae flowers are trimerous (3+3 tepals, 3+3 stamens) with a superior ovary.

questions.stem: Which root modification is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: Rhizophora has pneumatophores, not leaf tendrils.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a stem modification?
questions.explanation: Carrot is a swollen tap root; ginger, onion and potato are stem modifications.

questions.stem: Whorled phyllotaxy, with more than two leaves at a node, is seen in
questions.explanation: Alstonia (and Nerium) show whorled leaves; mustard/china rose are alternate; guava is opposite.

questions.stem: The pitcher of Nepenthes is a modification of the
questions.explanation: The lamina is modified into a pitcher; the leaf tip forms the lid.

questions.stem: In a cymose inflorescence the main axis
options: ends in a flower and growth is definite
questions.explanation: Cymose growth is determinate; the oldest flower is terminal and later flowers are basipetal.

questions.stem: In guava the ovary is inferior because the flower is
questions.explanation: In epigynous flowers (guava, cucumber, sunflower) the thalamus encloses the ovary.

questions.stem: Valvate aestivation, in which sepals or petals just touch without overlapping, occurs in
questions.explanation: Calotropis shows valvate aestivation; pea is vexillary; china rose and cotton are twisted.

questions.stem: An apocarpous gynoecium, with free carpels, is found in
questions.explanation: Lotus, rose and Michelia have free carpels; mustard and tomato are syncarpous.

questions.stem: Free-central placentation is characteristic of
questions.explanation: Ovules arise on a central column in a unilocular ovary (Caryophyllaceae, Primulaceae).

questions.stem: Epipetalous stamens and a swollen placenta are typical of
questions.explanation: Solanaceae (brinjal, tomato, Datura) have five epipetalous stamens and bicarpellary ovaries with swollen placentae.

questions.stem: A unisexual flower that bears only stamens is described as
questions.explanation: Staminate flowers have stamens only; pistillate flowers have carpels only.

questions.stem: Which placentation–example pair is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Tomato has axile placentation in a multilocular ovary; parietal is mustard/Argemone.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect floral character for Solanaceae.
options: Diadelphous stamens and a legume fruit
questions.explanation: Diadelphous stamens and legumes belong to Fabaceae, not Solanaceae.
